$comment: Distribution package names for the commands declared in
config/vshell/dependencies.json. scripts/gen-package-metadata.py joins the
two files and regenerates the optional-dependency blocks in the packaging
recipes, so the feature manifest and the packaging cannot drift apart.
Every command in dependencies.json must appear in "commands" or the
generator fails. Use "skip" for commands already covered by a hard
dependency or shipped inside the package. Omit a distro key when the
distribution has no package for that command; the entry is then left out of
that distribution's recipe rather than guessed at.
Package names were verified against archlinux.org, packages.debian.org
(trixie), the Fedora rawhide metadata API, and packages.gentoo.org.
Commands that back first-class, non-optional UI. optdepends/Suggests are
not installed by default by pacman, paru, apt or dnf, so a command that a
default bar button or modal points at cannot be advertised that way: the
screenshot button would report missing tools on a stock install (VGS-53).
The line is: does a default-configuration bar button or modal point at
it. Genuinely opt-in integrations (rclone, tailscale, greetd, bandwhich,
gpu-screen-recorder, pywalfox, zoxide, ffmpegthumbnailer, satty,
tesseract) stay optional and must stay absent-tolerant in the UI.
tailscale in particular must never become a hard dependency: it is a
network daemon with its own account and system service.
Terminals are deliberately absent: eight are listed as alternatives and
packaging has no way to express "any one of these". That needs an
xdg-terminal-exec style resolver, tracked separately.
"base" lists the per-distribution hard dependencies that do not come from
a manifest command (the runtime itself and its interpreters), in the order
they should appear ahead of the generated ones.
"unsupported" waives a required command on a distribution that has no
package for it. It is mandatory: without a waiver the generator fails
rather than quietly leaving the command out of one recipe, which would
ship exactly the broken stock install this list exists to prevent. Each
waiver is printed on every run, and goes stale loudly — declaring one for
a command the mapping does package is an error.

hyprpicker.gentoo: not packaged: packages.gentoo.org returns no hyprpicker in ::gentoo (checked 2026-08-04), so the ebuild can neither require nor advertise it. Capture and OCR under Hyprland report it missing on Gentoo until an ebuild exists.

sudo.nix: on NixOS the working sudo is the setuid wrapper in /run/wrappers/bin; putting pkgs.sudo on the wrapper's PATH prefix would shadow it with a binary that cannot elevate, which is worse than not providing one.

visudo.nix: ships with the same package as sudo, and is waived for the same reason.

$comment: org.freedesktop.Notifications is a first-come, first-served session bus
name, so two notification daemons on one session is not a supported
configuration (VGS-56). Every channel has to say so, and every channel
was saying something slightly different: Fedora named all four, Arch and
Debian omitted dunst, Gentoo and Void omitted swaync. Some of that is
correct — a virtual name can cover a daemon — and some of it was drift.
This section is the one list. Gentoo's blockers live inside the generated
RDEPEND, so they are generated from here; the other channels declare
conflicts in file-specific shapes and are verified against it instead, so
a daemon dropped from one recipe fails the run rather than shipping.
A daemon with no package on a channel must be waived, with the reason —
the same rule as required.unsupported.

notification-daemon.gentoo: Gentoo has no notification-daemon virtual; the daemons are blocked by name instead.
notification-daemon.void: xbps has no virtual package for notification daemons; they are conflicted by name instead.

dunst.arch: dunst provides the notification-daemon virtual on Arch, which is already conflicted.
dunst.debian: dunst Provides: notification-daemon on Debian, which is already conflicted.

swaync.gentoo: not packaged: packages.gentoo.org returns no swaync or SwayNotificationCenter in ::gentoo (checked 2026-08-04).
